question: Should OpenClaw core accept a new opt-in `channels.whatsapp.progressMessages` config surface for standalone WhatsApp progress texts, or should WhatsApp long-turn status stay within existing lifecycle/status/progress abstractions for now?
rationale: The repo policy sets a high bar for new config surfaces, and this PR adds channel/account config for a user-visible message-cadence feature without an issue or maintainer product signal.

options.title: Accept After Repair And Proof
options.body: Allow the new config surface if the ordering bug, docs map, and live WhatsApp proof are fixed before merge.

options.title: Narrow To Existing Progress Model
options.body: Ask the author to reuse or extend existing progress/status abstractions instead of adding a WhatsApp-only config object.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Close or pause this PR until a maintainer-sponsored issue defines the desired WhatsApp long-turn UX.

recommendation.title: Accept After Repair And Proof
recommendation.body: Allow the new config surface if the ordering bug, docs map, and live WhatsApp proof are fixed before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged WhatsApp config, delivery, and QA work is the closest current ownership signal for this channel behavior.
